topic: Law change: compulsory BIS hallmarking of gold jewellery extended to 398 districts in 26 States/UTs (up from 392) - six districts added: West Champaran (Bihar), South West Delhi, Panchmahal (Gujarat), Bulandshahr and Sant Kabir Nagar (UP), Rudraprayag (Uttarakhand); UP now 41 districts; hallmark = BIS logo, purity grade, 6-character HUID, check on BIS CARE app; exemptions incl. under 2 g, bullion, export, jewellers up to Rs 40 lakh turnover (Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery and Gold Artefacts (Fourth Amendment) Order, 2026, S.O. 5997(E) dated 2 Nov 2026, Gazette 3 Nov 2026, Ministry of Consumer Affairs with BIS, under BIS Act, 2016)

slides.title: Hallmark rule now in **398 districts**
slides.subtitle: Six more districts, including **Bulandshahr** and **Sant Kabir Nagar** in UP, now need hallmarked gold jewellery.
slides.cite: **Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery and Gold Artefacts (Fourth Amendment) Order, 2026** · S.O. 5997(E) · 2 Nov 2026

slides.label: What is new
slides.title: Six **new districts** added
bullets: The Consumer Affairs Ministry, with BIS, has replaced the district list in the **2020 Hallmarking Order**. It now covers **398 districts** in 26 States and UTs, up from 392.
New: **West Champaran** (Bihar), **South West Delhi**, **Panchmahal** (Gujarat), **Bulandshahr** and **Sant Kabir Nagar** (UP), **Rudraprayag** (Uttarakhand).
It applied from publication in the Gazette on **3 November 2026**. UP now has **41 districts** on the list.

slides.label: What it means
slides.title: Check the **hallmark** first
bullets: In these districts, registered jewellers must sell gold jewellery and artefacts only with a **BIS hallmark**.
A hallmark has three parts: the **BIS logo**, the **purity grade** (e.g. **22K916** = 22 carat) and a **6-character HUID** code unique to that piece.
Type the HUID into the free **BIS CARE** app to check the purity, the jeweller and the testing centre.
slides.note: If a hallmarked piece tests below its stamped purity, the buyer is entitled to **twice the value** of the shortfall plus the testing cost.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: Not every piece is **covered**
bullets: Exempt even in listed districts: pieces under **2 grams**, gold bullion, articles for **export**, and jewellers with yearly turnover up to **Rs 40 lakh**, among others.
If your district is not on the list, the hallmark is not yet compulsory there, but you can still ask for hallmarked gold.
Ask for a bill showing **net gold weight**, **purity** and the **hallmarking charge**. This post is for information only, not legal advice.

caption:
Buying gold? Check for the hallmark first 💍🔍

The Centre has extended compulsory hallmarking of gold jewellery to 398 districts across 26 States and Union Territories, up from 392. The six districts newly added are West Champaran (Bihar), South West Delhi, Panchmahal (Gujarat), Bulandshahr and Sant Kabir Nagar (Uttar Pradesh), and Rudraprayag (Uttarakhand). Uttar Pradesh now has 41 districts on the list. The change applied from its publication in the Gazette on 3 November 2026.

In listed districts, registered jewellers must sell gold jewellery and artefacts only with a BIS hallmark. A hallmark has three parts: the BIS logo, the purity grade (for example, 22K916 means 22 carat) and a six-character HUID code unique to that piece. You can enter the HUID in the free BIS CARE app to check the purity, the jeweller and the testing centre. If a hallmarked piece tests below its stamped purity, the buyer is entitled to twice the value of the shortfall plus the testing cost.

Some items are exempt even in listed districts, such as pieces under 2 grams, gold bullion, articles meant for export, and jewellers with a yearly turnover of up to Rs 40 lakh. Always ask for a bill showing the net gold weight, purity and hallmarking charge.

Law: Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery and Gold Artefacts (Fourth Amendment) Order, 2026, S.O. 5997(E) dated 2 November 2026, issued under the BIS Act, 2016
Issued by: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, with BIS

This post is for information only, not legal advice.
